objective: Determine whether a natural-sounding, offline, on-device (mobile) Urdu text-to-speech can ship under 10 MB total (model weights + any inference library we must bundle), and recommend the most viable concrete architecture + runtime + data path to get there. This is a feasibility-and-direction study that will decide the project's whole architecture.
done_when: You deliver: (1) a clear VERDICT on feasibility — is natural Urdu TTS under 10 MB incl. runtime achievable, and if not, what the tightest achievable (size, quality) point is; (2) a recommended stack named concretely — acoustic model/architecture, vocoder if separate, mobile inference runtime, and a MB-by-MB budget breakdown showing the total under 10 MB (or the closest real number); (3) at least one concrete Urdu data or pretrained-model source with a link and license; (4) 1-2 named fallback options with their size/quality tradeoff. Every size and capability claim carries a citation.
context: ["Project is UrduTTS, a cold/empty repo at the workspace root. boundaries: ["Do not write production code or a paper — this is a research report to direct the build.", "Do not recommend cloud/server inference or multi-language scope; both are out.", "Do not silently accept the 10 MB as impossible and pivot to parametric — if natural+10MB is truly out of reach, say so explicitly with the evidence and give the closest achievable point.", "Distinguish clearly what counts against the 10 MB (shipped bytes) vs what rides on the OS."]
budget: Worth a solid focused study. Stop and report once you can defend a recommended stack with a size budget and a data source; if a critical number (e.g. quantized model quality on Urdu) has no published source, say so rather than guessing.
